title: Effect of Feedback of Massive Stars in the Fragmentation, Distribution, and Kinematics of the Gas in Two Star-forming Regions in the Carina Nebula
question: How does stellar feedback from massive stars affect fragmentation, gas distribution and kinematics in two Carina Nebula regions (Northern Cloud vs Southern Pillars)?

data.sensitivity: 10 mJy/beam per channel; continuum 0.22 mJy/beam (NC), 0.12 mJy/beam (SP)

evidence.quote: assuming dust temperature values of 23 K for the SP and 28 K for the NC, both reported in (cite: 2016MNRAS.456.2406R)

evidence.loc: 4.2 Fraction of the mass in cores
evidence.quote: using the gas column density map derived in (cite: 2016MNRAS.456.2406R) from Herschel maps

recipe.method: Combined imaging of both arrays with tclean
key_parameters: robust 0.5; channel width 0.41 km/s for main lines

recipe.method: 2D Gaussian plus offset fitted to each core
key_parameters: cores kept only if S/N > 10 in NC

recipe.method: Dust continuum mass with fixed temperature and opacity
assumptions: T = 23 K (SP), 28 K (NC); gas-to-dust 100; beta=2; d=2.3 kpc

recipe.goal: Core velocity dispersion and virial parameter
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to H13CO+ core spectra; alpha_vir = 5 dv^2 R/(G M)
assumptions: uniform density, no magnetic fields or external pressure

recipe.method: Jeans mass from ATLASGAL-derived density in 20" radius sphere and dust temperature
SCIMES dendrograms on HCO+ and H13CO+ cubes; K-S and t-tests on leaf velocity dispersions
PCA on HCO+ cubes giving size-linewidth; Bayesian MCMC regression for alpha
Feather ALMA with ATLASGAL (immerge), build N-PDF, fit log-normal, infer Mach number

evidence.quote: While the NC has a mean core mass of 19.4 $\mbox{$M_{\odot}$}$, the mean in the SP is 3.8 $\mbox{$M_{\odot}$}$
the mean in the SP is 3.8 $\mbox{$M_{\odot}$}$

answer_key.quantity: mean HCO+ leaf velocity dispersion NC / SP

evidence.quote: The mean velocity dispersion is 0.37 $\mbox{km s$^{-1}$}$ for the NC, white for the SP is 0.31 $\mbox{km s$^{-1}$}$.
the peak value is 0.59 and a 90% HDI of \[0.37,0.75\] in the NC
peak at 0.34 for the SP, with a 90% HDI of \[0.01,0.52\]

answer_key.quantity: N-PDF transition column density NC / SP

evidence.quote: In the NC, the $N_\mathrm{H2,log}$ is $\sim 3.2\times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, while in the SP the $N_\mathrm{H2,log}$ is $\sim 1.7\times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$
Table [\[log-normal-fit\]](#log-normal-fit) shows a value of $\delta_\mathrm{H2}=0.62$ for the NC. In contrast, for the SP $\delta_\mathrm{H2}=0.39$.
This imply a $\mathcal{M}=1.37$ for the NC and $\mathcal{M}=0.81$ for the SP
